doc.title: James Moody interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

chapter: Race and racism on the road
title: Ella Fitzgerald tour arriving late
summary: On a tour with Ella Fitzgerald, the club owner wanted her to sing for his wife after a late arrival.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well I was on the bus when we were doing a tour with Ella Fitzgerald and we were late for the gig, about two hours late, and we pulled up to the place, like I mean everybody had gone and all like that. And the guy pointed to Ella Fitzgerald, she had her hair all wrapped up in her thing, and she wasn’t feeling well, tired, and the owner of the place wanted her to sing for his wife. I mean we finally got out of it, but I mean he wanted her to sing.
